tables.title: Arithmetic Invariants · Construction and Meaning
tables.intro: The kernel extends through distinct readers of the same structure. Residues and torsion determine characters; their moments produce spectral constants. Regularization preserves the finite parts of those moments. Compatible cylinders then allow resolutions and information rates to be compared. The recognized formulas come at the end of these constructions. Sources: the integral corpus, chapters 41–45, and the systematic treatise.
columns: Construction and Function of the Reader
grid: Third moment of the spectral counter; the trace realizes ζ(3) = 4π² log A₂.
Finite part of the regional decomposition C₀ + C₁ + C₂, after separating the divergent term.
Hierarchy of finite parts of the regional reader; they are recognized as Laurent coefficients of ζ at 1.
The oriented tritic character χ₋₃ supplies the logarithmic correction γ + L′(1,χ)/L(1,χ).
First level of regularized spectral products: exp[1/12 − ζ′(−1)].
Second level of the same hierarchy: log A₂ = −ζ′(−2) = ζ(3)/(4π²).
The prime-number reading separates repeated powers: γ − Σₖ≥₂ P(k)/k, where P is the prime zeta function.
Product of local exclusion factors for pairs differing by two: p(p − 2)/(p − 1)², p > 2.
The cylinders project onto continued fractions; their Gauss reading yields the typical geometric mean of the partial quotients.
In the same Gauss reading, the typical rate of denominator growth: π²/(12 log 2).
Ratio between base-b resolution and Gauss entropy: 6 log 2 log b / π².
Dodecaphasic unimodal profile: ratio between consecutive bifurcation intervals, level 14.
In the same profile, ratio between successive spatial distances, level 14.
tables.note: Khinchin, Lévy and Lochs describe rates for almost every trajectory under the Gauss measure. Feigenbaum is evaluated at level 14 of the sequence of approximants. Each numeral retains the reader and the domain that produce it; the detailed derivation includes the corresponding operators, convergence and bounds.
